title: RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking
author: Valentin Six, Mufei Li, Dongqi Fu, Yinglong Xia, Hong Li, Pan Li
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Different retrievers exist for retrieval-augmented generation, yet none performs best for all queries. Therefore, the key question is: given a query and retrieved passages from different retrievers, which one is most suited for that query? Existing routers usually make predictions from query-specific features and a fixed pool of retrievers; such routers have no output for an unseen retriever and are incapable by design on a new corpus. To fill these gaps, RAGCompass reads the retrieved passage sets themselves: passages from an unfamiliar retriever or corpus stay directly comparable to other passages, so routing stays well designed where a query-only map would fail. We contrastively fine-tune a reranker against the answer each evidence set produces, which accounts for most of the gain; a small comparison head adds a moderate improvement, and neither component has retriever-specific parameters. RAGCompass improves answer F1 by 28% relative to the best fixed retriever, and outperforms fusion baselines, three query-only routers, and a prompted 8B language model. Generalization experiments show that RAGCompass keeps most of its gain under an unseen corpus, retriever, or reader, while query-only baselines fall to the best fixed retriever or below.

title: Contextual Pictograms for Repairing Multilingual ASR Errors
author: Mariana Hernandez, Hector Luna, Carlos Bruno, Luis Ricardo Santos, Elena Simoes
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speech transcription errors can be difficult to recognize when competing word hypotheses are unfamiliar or visually similar. We describe an interface that combines alternative transcripts, replay and contextually checked pictograms for selected uncertain concepts. The system will initially support French and Spanish functional utterances. A counterbalanced study will assess whether pictorial feedback helps listeners recover the speaker's intended action beyond text alternatives alone. We will also quantify semantic mismatch and additional interaction time, since an inappropriate image can reinforce the wrong interpretation rather than repair it.

takeaways: A counterbalanced study will assess whether pictorial feedback helps listeners recover the speaker's intended action beyond text alternatives alone.
We will also quantify semantic mismatch and additional interaction time, since an inappropriate image can reinforce the wrong interpretation rather than repair it.

title: Cognitive Bias Signatures in Search-Equipped LLM Agents: A Stage-Resolved Analysis
author: Yanru Xiao, Yingwei Yu
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Search can help LLM agents correct mistakes, but their starting conditions may shape which evidence they find and use. Drawing on cognitive-bias paradigms, we develop a controlled search harness to examine result order, records of prior work, and initial hypotheses while holding each question and document collection fixed. Matched controls distinguish order effects from differences in document composition and the effects of failed work from context length. Across 10 models and 1,000 synthetic search worlds, we track queries, retrieved documents, document openings, and final answers. Our comparisons suggest that final answers are more sensitive to initial evidence order during active search than when all evidence is supplied in full. Dead-end histories can reduce strategy switching relative to matched neutral histories, indicating an effect beyond context length. Under wrong hypotheses, stage measurements distinguish reduced retrieval or opening from errors that persist after counter-evidence is opened. Exploratory interventions show that opening counter-evidence more often can coincide with lower accuracy, while accuracy can improve with little change in opening.

title: Prospective Memory for Proactive LLM Agents
author: Yuanchen Bei, Zhining Liu, Tianxin Wei, Weizhi Zhang, Zhichen Zeng, Philip S. Yu, Hendrik Hamann, Jingrui He, Hanghang Tong
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most memory systems for LLM agents are retrospective, preserving and retrieving past information to inform current decisions. Proactive agents, however, also require prospective memory: retaining future-directed intentions and realizing them when appropriate opportunities arise, even without explicit requests. Crucially, remembering the right intention does not guarantee acting at the right time: a related observation may call for waiting, while a later cue may make the same intention actionable. Inspired by cognitive theories of human prospective memory, we introduce Pro-Memory, a memory framework that separates maintaining future intentions from deciding when and how to realize them. Pro-Memory preserves pending objectives linked to their supporting evidence, assesses new observations against their original goals and activation conditions, and coordinates appropriate contributions with the agent's ongoing actions. It further updates intention states based on actions actually issued or evidence of resolution, while an experience memory distills feedback from completed episodes into guidance for future decisions. Experiments on two benchmarks spanning delayed-intention tasks and open-ended proactive assistance demonstrate consistent improvements in proactive task performance over representative memory approaches across multiple LLM backbones, while limiting unnecessary interventions.

title: How Well Can Large Language Models Impersonate Individual Authors? A Comparative Evaluation
author: Harshit Gupta, Shunichi Ishihara
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study investigates the authorship impersonation capacity of six widely used large language models (LLMs): Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Opus, GPT 5.2, GPT 5.2 Pro, DeepSeek 3.2, and Grok 4.1 Fast. The evaluation was conducted using short product review texts selected to ensure high within author consistency in individual writing style. Two types of in context prompt were designed: a simple prompt with minimal instruction and a complex prompt incorporating explicit stylometric guidance for mimicry. Authorship mimicry was evaluated using a cosine distance based distance to training metric, supplemented by visual analyses of embedding distributions. The results indicate that authorship impersonation remained challenging for most LLMs, with Gemini 3 Pro showing the strongest apparent mimicry performance. However, subsequent overlap analysis revealed that Gemini 3 Pro extensively copied and reused sentences and phrases from the training texts, at levels far exceeding those observed among human authors. Follow up factor analyses showed that training set consistency was the most robust predictor of mimicry success across models, whereas author distinctiveness did not generalise as a reliable predictor. Global embedding visualisations further revealed a consistent macro level pattern: for most models, generated texts occupied regions of the embedding space that were largely separated from the corresponding human training clusters. This indicates limited convergence towards target author style and suggests the presence of model specific lexical and phraseological preferences. The findings highlight the importance of distinguishing genuine stylistic imitation from direct textual reuse and have implications for the forensic analysis of textual evidence involving potential LLM enabled impersonation.

title: Phonological Knowledge of Chinese Characters in Language Models
author: Xiaozhe Ji, Renfen Hu, Hai Hu
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How much phonological knowledge do language models (LMs) possess about Chinese characters, and how is this knowledge represented and used? We introduce PinyinBench, a controlled benchmark covering homophones, phonological features (initials, finals, and tones), and polyphonic characters. We investigate 17 text-only and multimodal LMs through three complementary approaches: behavioral evaluation, layer-wise probing, and activation steering. Behaviorally, models demonstrate substantial knowledge of initials and finals, with a frontier model (DS-v4-flash) scoring 90%+ in homophone judgment, when two characters share no phonological features. However, its accuracy drops sharply to 72% when two characters differ only in lexical tone. Probing reveals that tone is highly decodable from embeddings and improves modestly across layers, whereas segmental information starts less decodable and improves substantially with depth. Activation steering shows that segmental representations can systematically influence generation, while tone exhibits much weaker effects. Furthermore, audio-bearing training improves phonological decodability, including tone, without corresponding improvements in steering effectiveness. Together, these findings reveal distinct representational and functional profiles for segmental and tonal information, with tonal information much harder to access and manipulate, demonstrating the necessity for combined evaluation, probing, and causal intervention for understanding linguistic knowledge in LMs.

title: Matching the Training-Time Weight Rule in Inference-Time Expert Deactivation
author: Hao Cheng (Zhejiang Gongshang University), Zhiyu Yang (Chang'an University), Bo Ma (Zhejiang Gongshang University), Hanzhang Jia (University of Sussex)
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Expert deactivation at inference time changes both token routing and expert weights, and its effect on performance depends on how these changes are implemented. We compare removal, freezing, remaining-expert renormalization, and unnormalized re-routing on identical disabled sets across five instruction-tuned checkpoints from four model families, with a base OLMoE checkpoint as an additional comparison. We develop a weight-sum model that relates the loss of expert contributions and changes in branch scale to the weight rule used during training. With half of the experts deactivated according to activation-based rankings, remaining-expert renormalization yields the highest perplexity in models trained with raw router probabilities, whereas unnormalized re-routing yields the highest perplexity in models trained with normalized weights. Perplexity ranges from 1.4 to 73 times the intact baseline when the training rule is retained, and from 14 to 28,740 times the baseline under a rule mismatch. Task outcomes vary across evaluation types: on OLMoE, GSM8K strict-match accuracy falls to zero under all four implementations. Extending the model to changes in the number of active experts yields a further prediction, supported by the OLMoE experiments: the perplexity penalty from additional renormalization increases as fewer experts are activated.

title: Learning When Human Decisions Matter: Executor-Relative Consultation Value for LLM Agents
author: Shuli Jiang, Khushbu Pahwa, Yuting Zhang, Yi Zhang, Wei Xia, Stefano Soatto
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models increasingly automate complex tasks, but human decision capacity does not scale with their capabilities. In many applications, humans remain essential for providing private context, authority, or judgments unavailable to the agent. We formulate human decision capacity allocation: given multiple consultation opportunities and a limited budget, at which decisions should an LLM agent consult a human? The central challenge is estimating consultation value, which is executor-dependent because the same human input may benefit different downstream agents differently. We introduce Consultation Value Distillation (CVD), which estimates consultation values offline using Monte Carlo executor rollouts and distills these values into lightweight predictors for budgeted allocation, requiring no rollout-based value estimation at deployment. Across five batch and three sequential settings with two frontier executors, CVD improves allocation through joint and continuation-aware value learning, while independent consultation values remain competitive in several settings. CVD also broadly outperforms direct prompting and Value of Information where applicable, remains robust with substantially less rollout supervision, and enables nearly lossless approximate allocation at low search cost.

title: TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi-Agent Collaboration
author: Baohang Li, Xiaocheng Feng, Bing Qin
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision models choose among predefined options in tasks such as routing and action selection. In multi-agent collaboration, a decision determines how members divide work, exchange resources, and act in parallel. We introduce TandemBench, a benchmark of 1,200 questions in multi-agent cooking scenarios where coordination choices affect goal completion. Models receive complete global information and candidate team plans, with reference answers established through execution and exact search. Models select an optimal team plan and, in paired variants that retain or remove it, judge whether better arrangements exist beyond the supplied options. We evaluate 40 native decision models and compare them with 10 general-purpose language models. The best native decision model achieves 62.50% decision accuracy. Native decision models remain close to chance in optimality verification. Paired tests reveal that some report better alternatives regardless of whether an optimal plan is already present. These findings show that team-plan decision accuracy alone can conceal systematic errors in judging whether the supplied options contain an optimal arrangement. The dataset and evaluation code are publicly available at https://github.com/lililibaohang/TandemBench.

title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines
author: Yuqin Dai, Zhanwei Zhang, Honghui Yang, Zhouheng Yao, Yueqi Zhang, Jingyu He, Chaoyang Shi, Fanding Wei, Boyuan Pan, Kai Xu, Yao Hu, Yongliang Shen
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) shopping assistants now recommend products in multi-turn conversations. However, reliable evaluation faces Data scarcity and Difficulty Standardizing Criteria. To address these obstacles, we introduce CARTBench for CART (Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines). For Data scarcity, we curate cases from real commercial shopping needs across 17 retail domains, pairing timestamped dialogue with 1,603 product records. For Difficulty Standardizing Criteria, we develop case-specific rubrics guided by Ideal Response Principles, distilled from excellent replies manually selected from successfully completed orders. These principles also guide Principle-Guided CART Prompting, our structured recommendation strategy. The experimental benchmark contains 1,328 expert-annotated criteria across Core, Excellence, and Safety. To answer the CART question, we evaluate 7 flagship commercial API models, including GPT-6.1-Sol and Claude-Opus-5, and 35B+ parameters open-weight models. In the first full-suite evaluation under the frozen rubrics, 3 of 10 models exceed 90% on Core, while none exceeds 45% on Excellence. Therefore, we identify an understanding-to-execution gap between required behavior and high-quality purchase advice. To examine these limitations, we diagnose shared failures in product evidence and unresolved needs, linked to changing requirements and decisive unknowns. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Da1yuqin/CARTBench.

title: When Does Better Confidence Improve a Knowledge-Graph Audit?
author: Zehao Lin, Kai Chen, Xixuan Hao, Erenkai Zhu, Chunyu Li, Helan Hu
contentSnippet: arXiv:2611.05877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Confidence estimates guide human review in LLM-built knowledge graphs, but better error prediction can yield little improvement in an audit. We study this gap through repairability, selection headroom and label validity. Modelling non-adaptive auditing as budgeted covering, we characterise the minimal decision-relevant error statistics and bound the regret of scalar-preserving first-order planning by a structural mass $\Delta^{\mathrm{cl}}$. We simulate ideal repair against benchmark-aligned labels for five extraction configurations and two cross-document graphs on Re-DocRED, followed by frozen confirmation on test and replication on 500 hash-selected training documents. On the held-out cross-document graphs, an error-rate $\times$ fan-out queue leaves 3.98-4.74 percentage points more errors than a joint model with the same actions. By comparison, opening shared actions for that joint planner reduces residual errors by 0.89-1.43 points relative to its own fact-only plans, in point estimates. Equivalence between joint and independent-block models remains inconclusive. Generic LLM verification improves three of four model-budget configurations on each held-out set. LLM adjudication identifies possible benchmark omissions.

title: Kyndryl shares surge 30% on hyperscaler-related revenue growth
author: Maria Deutscher
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 20:33 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026

Kyndryl shares surge 30% on hyperscaler-related revenue growth

Shares of Kyndryl Holdings Inc. jumped 30% today after it reported better-than-expected earnings for the second quarter of its 2027 fiscal year.

Kyndryl generated $3.9 billion in sales during the three months ended Sept. 30. That represents a 1.9% decrease from a year earlier, but the company still managed to top the consensus estimate by about $50 million. It attributed the top-line surprise to its Kyndryl Consult business.

Kyndryl, a former IBM Corp. unit, once generated nearly all its revenue from managing other companies’ technology infrastructure. In 2022, it launched Kyndryl Consult to take on more strategic, higher-margin professional services deals.

The unit’s revenue grew 4.2% year-over-year in the second quarter. Kyndryl didn’t share a specific quarterly revenue number, but divulged that the unit earned a total of $3.6 billion over the past 12 months.

Kyndryl Consult’s signings, a measure of future revenue, jumped 19% over the past year. That momentum may have contributed to the company’s stock rally today.

Many of the projects that Kyndryl Consult takes on involve artificial intelligence. The unit can help customers build AI agent ensembles and set up training data generation pipelines. Additionally, it can advise clients about business decisions such as how they should allocate their AI budgets.

Kyndryl offers a software platform called Bridge to companies that buy its AI services. It enables AI agents to access business data from an organization’s internal systems. Additionally, Bridge monitors those agents to ensure they adhere to safety requirements.

The public cloud is another major focus of Kyndryl’s growth efforts. The company’s hyperscale-related revenue topped $500 million in the second quarter, which amounts to a 27% year-over-year increase.

“Strong signings and continued growth in Kyndryl Consult and hyperscaler-related revenue reinforce our confidence in our fiscal 2027 outlook,” said Kyndryl Chief Executive Officer Martin Schroeter. “Our performance reflects demand for Kyndryl’s AI-led modernization capabilities and deep mission-critical expertise that help customers evolve their complex technology environments, strengthen cybersecurity and achieve measurable business outcomes.”

The company delivered an adjusted net income of

summary.tldr:
Kyndryl Holdings Inc. shares rose 30% following a second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings report that exceeded analyst expectations. The company reported $3.9 billion in revenue for the quarter ending September 30, surpassing consensus estimates by $50 million despite a 1.9% year-over-year decline. Adjusted net income reached $92 million, or 42 cents per share, beating the 41-cent forecast. This performance was driven by the company's strategic pivot toward higher-margin professional services and cloud-related growth.

The Kyndryl Consult unit, launched in 2022 to move beyond legacy infrastructure management, saw revenue grow 4.2% year-over-year, with $3.6 billion in total revenue over the trailing 12 months and a 19% increase in new signings. A significant portion of this growth is attributed to AI-led modernization projects, including the development of AI agent ensembles and data pipelines. The company supports these deployments with its 'Bridge' software platform, which facilitates agent access to internal business data and provides safety monitoring. Additionally, hyperscaler-related revenue grew 27% year-over-year, exceeding $500 million for the quarter.

Kyndryl is currently executing a cost-reduction program, which included a $38 million workforce reduction charge in the second quarter. This initiative is projected to generate $500 million in annual savings starting in fiscal year 2028. For the remainder of fiscal 2027, the company forecasts adjusted pretax income between $600 million and $700 million, with revenue expected to remain flat or grow by up to 2%.
takeaways: **Financial Performance:** Kyndryl reported $3.9 billion in Q2 revenue and $92 million in adjusted net income (42 cents per share).
**Consulting Growth:** The Kyndryl Consult unit recorded a 19% year-over-year increase in signings and $3.6 billion in revenue over the last 12 months.
**Cloud Expansion:** Hyperscaler-related revenue grew 27% year-over-year, surpassing the $500 million mark for the quarter.
**Cost Optimization:** A workforce reduction charge of $38 million was taken in Q2 as part of a plan to achieve $500 million in annual savings by fiscal 2028.
**AI Infrastructure:** The company's 'Bridge' platform is used to manage AI agent access to internal systems and enforce safety compliance.

title: Apple is reportedly cutting budgets for its internal AI usage
author: Lucas Ropek
contentSnippet: Posted: 5:26 PM PST · November 4, 2026 Image Credits: STR/NurPhoto / Getty Images Lucas Ropek Apple is reportedly cutting budgets for its internal AI usage Apple is cutting the daily amount its engineering teams can spend on AI, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. It’s a big change for a company that has worked to integrate the technology into its engineering processes. In October, Apple lowered the daily AI spending cap for its engineering teams, decreasing it from $300 to $200, the outlet reported. And more cuts are in the works, with some allowances falling to $100 a day, sources tell Bloomberg. Outside engineering, Apple is reportedly weighing a daily limit as low as $25 a day. TechCrunch has reached out to Apple for comment. Earlier this year, a tsunami of tokenmaxxing took hold, with companies pushing staff to use AI as much as possible in the name of vaguely defined efficiency gains. The frenzy was short-lived, however, as bills for said tokens came due, and companies decided that token rationing might be a more fiscally sensible approach. Concerns persist about an apparent gap between what AI costs to build and run and the (often unclear) productivity gains the technology is suppose to generate. summary.tldr:
Apple has begun implementing strict daily spending caps on internal AI usage for its engineering teams, signaling a shift toward fiscal discipline regarding generative AI integration. According to reports, the company reduced the daily AI expenditure limit for engineers from $300 to $200 in October, with further reductions to $100 per day currently in progress.

Beyond the engineering department, Apple is reportedly evaluating even more restrictive measures, considering daily AI spending limits as low as $25 for other internal teams. This move reflects a broader industry trend where companies are moving away from unrestricted "tokenmaxxing"—the practice of maximizing AI usage for efficiency gains—as the actual costs of running large-scale AI models become clearer and the measurable productivity returns remain uncertain.
takeaways: **Engineering Spending Cap:** Apple reduced the daily AI budget for engineering teams from $300 to $200 in October.
**Planned Reductions:** Internal allowances for engineering teams are expected to drop further to $100 per day.
**Non-Engineering Limits:** Apple is considering implementing daily AI spending caps as low as $25 for staff outside of engineering.

**Industry Context:** The shift follows a period of aggressive AI adoption, with companies now prioritizing "token rationing" due to concerns over the gap between high operational costs and realized productivity gains.

title: After the midterms, a bigger clash over data centers could be coming
author: Dominic-Madori Davis
contentSnippet:
The November 3 midterm results gave Democrats full control of Congress, setting the stage for what could be one of the most divided U.S. governments this decade, with Republicans in the White House.

Tuesday’s results suggest that anger over data centers, the large facilities that house the computers powering AI, is becoming a political force. With Democrats now in control of Congress, that could lead to new limits on where data centers can be built and how much say local communities have.

Data centers became a ballot-box issue in various states. An NBC exit poll showed how concerned voters are about AI: More than half of respondents believe that AI will do more harm than good, while almost 80% are against the building of data centers in their neighborhoods. Almost 60%, meanwhile, said data centers were a crucial or major factor in their vote. Nadine Smith, president and CEO of the racial justice organization Color of Change, called Tuesday’s election a referendum on “who this economy is built for.”

“National security matters,” Smith said, referring to a common argument from data center supporters that the infrastructure is essential for the U.S. to stay ahead in war and in its rivalry with China. “And so do the families in South Memphis breathing exhaust from the gas turbines powering an AI supercomputer.” (She was referring to xAI’s data center in Memphis, Tennessee, which uses gas turbines for power.)

Voters in several states pushed back against the AI buildout, even as pro-AI super PACs spent millions hoping to sway them this midterm. The anti-data center backlash was especially felt in states like Ohio, where OpenAI has eyed a $500 billion data center, backed by more than $100 billion in financing from Nvidia. In fact, the Ohio county where Meta had planned a 700,000-square-foot facility just passed a ban on data centers, and local communities across the state overwhelmingly voted against data center buildout measures.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley predict that Democratic governor-elect Amy Acton will also pose a major risk to Ohio’s data center buildout. Elsewhere, candidates in Texas, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Georgia, and South Carolina all won seats after taking a stance against the rapid buildout of data centers. “It is clear that money does not buy outcomes,” said Aniketh Koneru, a tech and policy researcher, adding that in modern politics, creati

summary.tldr:
Following the November 3 midterm elections, the U.S. political landscape faces a significant shift regarding AI infrastructure, as data centers have emerged as a potent ballot-box issue. With Democrats securing control of Congress, there is increased momentum for legislative restrictions on data center siting, community approval requirements, and grid cost-sharing mandates. Public sentiment, as reflected in NBC exit polling, shows nearly 80% of voters oppose data center construction in their neighborhoods, with nearly 60% citing these facilities as a major factor in their voting decisions. This backlash persists despite significant spending by pro-AI super PACs.

Technically and economically, the conflict centers on the environmental impact and grid strain caused by high-density AI supercomputers, such as xAI’s Memphis facility, which utilizes gas turbines. Legislative proposals, including those from Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, advocate for a nationwide moratorium on new data centers until federal guardrails are established. Additionally, the GRID Savings Act, proposed by Sen. Martin Heinrich, seeks to prevent the transfer of grid infrastructure costs to local communities. Analysts at Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley anticipate construction delays in key states like Texas, Ohio, and Georgia as local governments and incoming officials, such as governor-elect Amy Acton, prioritize stricter oversight and potential moratoriums.
takeaways: **Public Sentiment:** NBC exit polls indicate 80% of voters oppose local data center construction, and 50% believe AI does more harm than good.
**Legislative Proposals:** Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez have proposed a nationwide moratorium on new data centers to ensure environmental compliance and community consent.

**Economic Impact:** Goldman Sachs predicts construction delays in Georgia and Texas due to Democratic gains, while the GRID Savings Act aims to shift grid upgrade costs from communities to developers.

**Regional Backlash:** Ohio has seen significant resistance, including a county-level ban on data centers and local opposition to a proposed $500 billion OpenAI facility backed by $100 billion in Nvidia financing.

**Infrastructure Concerns:** Opposition is driven by the use of gas turbines for power, as seen at xAI’s Memphis site, and the use of NDAs by tech companies to bypass public discourse during the planning phase.

title: AI PACs spent millions trying to shape Congress — here’s how they fared
author: Rebecca Bellan
contentSnippet:
Political groups both supporting and opposing the AI industry spent millions of dollars trying to influence Tuesday’s midterm elections and shape the future of AI regulation. That spending produced mixed results, with some of the most heavily backed candidates losing their races.

On the industry side, two AI-focused political action committees (PACs) that raised and spent money to influence the elections — American Mission and Building the Future — collectively spent $4.8 million to back South Carolina Senate candidate Darline Graham, who lost. American Mission is the Republican spending arm of Leading the Future (LTF), a broader political group backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and the VC firm Andreessen Horowitz.

American Mission also spent more than $500,000 apiece supporting Republican House candidates Aaron Flint in Montana and Laurie Buckhout in North Carolina, both of whom lost. LTF’s Democratic spending arm, Think Big, had better luck backing Florida Rep. Jared Moskowitz, who won reelection.

Groups advocating for stronger AI safeguards also saw mixed results. Public First, which is backed by Anthropic, supported several Republicans who lost through its affiliated PAC but had more success backing Democratic candidates. It also contributed $3 million to a PAC supporting California state Sen. Scott Wiener, who was leading his race at the time of publication.

Meanwhile, Guardrails Alliance , a group that has sought to make taking money from AI companies a political liability, spent more than $1 million apiece opposing two candidates who lost: California Rep. Jimmy Gomez and Montana’s Aaron Flint. It also spent $300,000 supporting Angela Gonzales-Torres, who defeated Gomez.

It’s difficult to separate the impact of AI-related spending from the broader Democratic wave that swept Tuesday’s elections. Elon Musk, who reportedly poured half a billion dollars into supporting Republicans in the midterms, also saw many of his candidates lose . Indeed, LTF also backed some candidates it believed were likely to win, only to see them lose to the Dems.

For LTF, though, the general election wasn’t the main focus. The group told TechCrunch ahead of Election Day that it thinks primaries (the contests that choose each party’s nominee) are a more effective use of its money, because spending there can build name recognition and help candidates set up AI policy

summary.tldr:
Political action committees (PACs) representing both the AI industry and AI-safety advocates saw mixed results in the recent midterm elections, with significant spending failing to guarantee candidate victories. Leading the Future (LTF), a group backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and Andreessen Horowitz, spent $4.8 million through its American Mission arm to support South Carolina Senate candidate Darline Graham, who lost. LTF also deployed over $500,000 each for unsuccessful House bids by Aaron Flint (Montana) and Laurie Buckhout (North Carolina), though its Democratic arm, Think Big, successfully supported the reelection of Florida Rep. Jared Moskowitz. LTF prioritized primary elections, spending $27.38 million in those contests, including $8 million to defeat New York Assembly member Alex Bores.

Conversely, the Guardrails Alliance, which aims to make AI-industry funding a political liability, spent over $1 million each to oppose candidates Jimmy Gomez and Aaron Flint, while contributing $300,000 to support Angela Gonzales-Torres, who defeated Gomez. Public First, backed by Anthropic, also engaged in the cycle, contributing $3 million to a PAC supporting California state Sen. Scott Wiener. The core legislative conflict driving this spending is the debate over whether Congress should establish a preemptive national AI framework or allow states to maintain independent regulatory authority. Both sides have signaled continued involvement in future election cycles, with LTF planning to participate in 2028 and the Guardrails Alliance continuing its strategy of framing AI-industry donations as toxic.
takeaways: **LTF Primary Spending:** Leading the Future spent $27.38 million during the primary season, significantly more than its general election expenditures.
**Guardrails Alliance Strategy:** The group spent over $1 million each to oppose Jimmy Gomez and Aaron Flint, specifically targeting candidates who accepted AI-industry funding.
**Legislative Conflict:** The primary policy divide centers on whether a federal AI framework should override state-level regulations.
**LTF Backers:** Leading the Future is supported by OpenAI president Greg Brockman and the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.
**Public First Contribution:** Anthropic-backed Public First contributed $3 million to a PAC supporting California state Sen. Scott Wiener.

title: Qualcomm is betting big on data centers as smartphone sales sink
author: Terrence O’Brien
contentSnippet: With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta announced earlier this year. The company expects that portion of its business to grow quickly, forecasting around $650 million in data center revenue during the first quarter of 2027. But it anticipates that will reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029. Considering the company’s total revenue for 2026 was $10.4 billion, that would constitute a significant share of its earnings. It confirmed during the call that it expects data centers to eventually account for around 30 percent of its business. That’s not quite as ambitious as AMD, which says that it expects over 80 percent of its revenue will eventually come from data centers. But it suggests there’s plenty of demand that needs to be filled and enough AI money to go around.

summary.tldr:
Qualcomm is pivoting toward the data center market to offset a 20 percent decline in smartphone sales compared to 2025. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company outlined a strategy to capture AI infrastructure market share, leveraging previously announced partnerships with Amazon and Meta. Qualcomm projects rapid growth in this segment, forecasting $650 million in data center revenue for Q1 2027, scaling to $5 billion by year-end 2027, and reaching $15 billion by 2029.

This transition represents a fundamental shift in Qualcomm's business model, as the company aims for data centers to eventually comprise 30 percent of its total revenue. While this target is less aggressive than AMD’s goal of deriving over 80 percent of its revenue from data centers, it underscores Qualcomm's attempt to diversify away from its 2026 total revenue base of $10.4 billion, which was heavily reliant on mobile hardware.
takeaways: **Revenue Forecasts:** Qualcomm projects data center revenue to hit $650 million in Q1 2027, $5 billion by the end of 2027, and $15 billion by 2029.
**Market Shift:** The company aims for data center operations to eventually account for 30 percent of its total business.
**Baseline Performance:** Qualcomm reported total revenue of $10.4 billion for 2026, alongside a 20 percent year-over-year decline in smartphone sales.
**Strategic Partnerships:** Growth plans are anchored by existing collaborations with Amazon and Meta announced earlier in 2026.

title: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones
author: Dan Goodin
contentSnippet: Hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws in an attempt to hack visitors of multiple websites, including one celebrating the 250th anniversary of American independence, researchers said Wednesday. The attackers, which the researchers assessed with “moderate to high confidence” were part of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service, targeted other sites, many with links to that country’s ongoing war against Ukraine. The attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites. JavaScript injected into the traffic then profiled the device. The final payloads, tailored to the type of platform visiting, attempted to steal browser cookies and, in some cases, Wi-Fi passwords and full mobile device data. Wielding DarkSword One of the impersonated sites was america250.org, belonging to a non-partisan group of lawmakers, business executives, and at least one former member of the Trump administration. The attackers registered america250[.]holiday and used it as a reverse proxy to america250.org. The imposter website delivered content from the real one that added malicious JavaScript into it. Read full article Comments

summary.tldr:
Researchers at security firm Sekoia have identified a sophisticated watering hole campaign, attributed with moderate-to-high confidence to Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR/APT29), targeting visitors of high-profile websites. The attackers utilized three primary infection vectors: direct JavaScript injection, the use of proxy domains (such as america250[.]holiday), and a supply-chain compromise of a Ukrainian web analytics service. Once a target visited a compromised site, injected JavaScript profiled the device, allowing the attackers to deploy zero-click exploit chains tailored to the specific platform.

The campaign specifically targeted sites with geopolitical significance, including america250.org and the website for the Raffles London at The OWO, a hotel frequently used by high-profile diplomatic delegations. The attackers leveraged 'n-day' vulnerabilities—flaws that had already been patched—meaning the exploits were only effective against users running outdated versions of iOS or Android. The payloads were designed to exfiltrate browser cookies, Wi-Fi passwords, and comprehensive mobile device data. One of the identified exploit kits, DarkSword, has previously been linked to the Turkish surveillance vendor PARS Defense.
takeaways: **Attribution:** Sekoia researchers attribute the campaign to Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service (APT29) based on target profiles and technical similarities to previous operations.
**Infection Vectors:** Attackers employed three methods: direct JavaScript injection, proxy domains (e.g., america250[.]holiday), and a supply-chain compromise of a Ukrainian web analytics service.
**Exploit Mechanism:** The campaign utilized zero-click exploit chains that required no user interaction, relying on 'n-day' vulnerabilities that only affected unpatched iOS and Android devices.

**Targeting Strategy:** The campaign focused on high-profile sites, including those related to the 250th anniversary of American independence and the Raffles London at The OWO, to target diplomatic and government-affiliated visitors.
**Payload Capabilities:** Successful exploits allowed attackers to steal browser cookies, Wi-Fi credentials, and full mobile device data.

title: webAI Releases TwIL-8B, an 8.8B Reasoning Model Scoring 98.2 on MATH-500
author: Asif Razzaq
contentSnippet: webAI has released TwIL-8B , an 8.8B reasoning model for math, code and instruction following. The TwIL-8B reasoning model is post-trained from IBM’s Granite 4.2 8B . Weights are on Hugging Face under a non-commercial license. webAI’s launch post frames the pitch around cost per task, not raw scale. The 4-bit build is 4.98 GiB, sized for CPU or modest-VRAM GPU inference. TL;DR Size: 8.79B parameters, dense. 131,072-token context, inherited from the base model. Runs on: CPU or modest-VRAM GPU via a 4.98 GiB Q4_K_M GGUF. Full bf16 weights are 16.38 GiB. Performance: Leads its size class on math and code, trails on knowledge benchmarks. Best: MATH-500 at 98.2, the top score in webAI’s comparison. Worst: GPQA Diamond at 70.2, 11.5 points behind Qwen3.5-9B. HLE is 12.6 (verbose variant). What is TwIL-8B? TwIL-8B is a dense decoder-only reasoning model from webAI. It has 40 layers, hidden size 4096, and 32 attention heads with 8 KV heads . Input and output are English text only. The model writes a <think> block before each answer. It ships in 2 variants with the same architecture and tokenizer. Balanced is the default and produces shorter reasoning traces. Verbose reasons longer and targets hard contest-style problems. TwIL-8B extends webAI’s TwIL family. The first members were 1.7B and 3B formal-logic models released in August 2026. How was TwIL-8B trained? webAI used 3 post-training stages : Full-parameter SFT on reasoning traces for math, STEM and instruction following. GRPO/DAPO reinforcement learning on math, code, STEM and instruction prompts. This produces the verbose variant. Length-aware RL with a reward that favors shorter traces against per-domain length references. This produces the balanced variant. Training pools were decontaminated with 13-gram matching against AIME, HMMT, MATH-500, GPQA and other evals. How does TwIL-8B perform on benchmarks? All TwIL-8B scores are self-reported, high-effort pass@1 with thinking enabled. Scores marked † were measured on the verbose variant only. Math : TwIL-8B scores 98.2 on MATH-500. Qwen3.5-9B lists 96.6 on a third-party leaderboard . Gemma 4 31B scored 87.9 in Red Hat’s lighteval run . On AIME 2025, TwIL-8B posts 88.3 against 87.1 for Gemma 4 31B. On AIME 2026 it scores 88.3, behind Qwen3.5-9B at 92.5 and Gemma 4 31B at 89.2 . Code : LiveCodeBench† is 81.6, against 65.6 for Qwen3.5-9B and 80.0 for Gemma 4 31B. w

summary.tldr:
webAI has released TwIL-8B, an 8.8B parameter dense reasoning model post-trained from IBM’s Granite 4.2 8B. Designed for math, code, and instruction following, the model is available on Hugging Face under a non-commercial license. It features a 131,072-token context window and is optimized for efficient deployment, with a 4-bit Q4_K_M GGUF version weighing 4.98 GiB, while the full bf16 weights occupy 16.38 GiB. The model architecture consists of 40 layers, a 4096 hidden size, 32 attention heads, and 8 KV heads.

TwIL-8B is offered in two variants: 'Balanced,' which produces shorter reasoning traces, and 'Verbose,' which targets complex contest-style problems. Training involved three stages: full-parameter SFT on STEM and instruction traces, GRPO/DAPO reinforcement learning, and length-aware RL to manage reasoning trace duration. The training data underwent 13-gram decontamination against benchmarks including AIME, HMMT, MATH-500, and GPQA. Performance is highlighted by a 98.2 score on MATH-500 and 88.3 on AIME 2025, though it trails competitors like Qwen3.5-9B on knowledge-heavy benchmarks such as GPQA Diamond, where it scored 70.2.
takeaways: **Model Architecture:** Dense decoder-only model with 8.79B parameters, 40 layers, 4096 hidden size, and 32 attention heads (8 KV heads).
**Benchmark Performance:** Achieved 98.2 on MATH-500 and 81.6 on LiveCodeBench (Verbose variant), outperforming Gemma 4 31B in these specific categories.
**Deployment Specs:** Available as a 4.98 GiB 4-bit GGUF for CPU/modest-VRAM inference or 16.38 GiB in full bf16 precision.
**Training Methodology:** Utilized three-stage post-training including full-parameter SFT, GRPO/DAPO reinforcement learning, and length-aware RL for trace optimization.
**Decontamination:** Training sets were filtered using 13-gram matching against AIME, HMMT, MATH-500, and GPQA to prevent benchmark leakage.

title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor, whose app runs several coding agents at once
author: Duncan Riley
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 17:20 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026

Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor, whose app runs several coding agents at once

Meta Platforms Inc. has acquired artificial intelligence coding startup Conductor in a deal first reported today by Axios .

Conductor confirmed it’s joining Meta in a post on its website . Terms were not disclosed.

The company’s software lets a developer run several coding agents at once, each in an isolated copy of the codebase, and then review and merge what they produce. Supported agents include Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code, OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex and Space Exploration Technologies Corp.’s Cursor, and users pay for them through their own subscriptions and keys.

The desktop app runs on Macs. A hosted version, Conductor Cloud, puts agents in sandboxed virtual machines where they can keep working for hours, and users can check on them from an iPhone app.

Engineers at Meta were using Conductor well before the deal. When the startup announced its Series A in March , it named Meta, Google LLC and Spotify Technology SA among the companies with dozens of engineers on the product. Conductor now says on its website that more than 100,000 people use it.

People familiar with the deal told Axios that Meta expects the Conductor team’s speed at shipping products to help it build its next generation of AI coding tools. The acquisition follows two Meta model releases last month that both pitched coding as a strength.

On Oct. 15 , Meta released Muse Spark Open, an open-weights version of its Muse Spark model aimed at coding and long-running agent work. Meta’s more capable Muse Wonder models stay closed inside its own Muse Code terminal and application programming interface.

The Conductor deal landed the same day OpenAI said it plans to acquire developer tools startup Pierre Computer. OpenAI had already announced plans in June to buy Ona, which runs coding agents in cloud sandboxes.

Conductor’s own products are closing in stages, starting with a halt today to new sign-ups and downloads. Pro subscribers now get their paid features free. The cloud service goes read-only on Nov. 13 and shuts on Nov. 20, after which the company will start deleting the data users stored there. Before that date, users can export their data or move cloud workspaces onto their own machines, and active subscribers will get refunds.

Local copies of the Mac app keep

summary.tldr:
Meta Platforms Inc. has acquired AI coding startup Conductor (formally Melty Inc., founded in 2024 by CEO Charlie Holtz and CTO Jackson de Campos), with financial terms left undisclosed. Conductor's software allows developers to execute multiple coding agents concurrently—supporting Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex, and Cursor—within isolated codebase copies, reviewing and merging their output. Prior to the acquisition, Conductor had raised a $22 million Series A in March led by Spark Capital and Matrix, with backing from Y Combinator and the founders of Notion and Linear. Meta engineers were already utilizing the product alongside users at Google and Spotify, helping push Conductor's user base past 100,000.

The acquisition coincides with Meta's recent product expansions in AI coding, following its mid-October release of the open-weights Muse Spark Open model for coding and long-running agents, alongside its closed Muse Wonder models accessible via the Muse Code terminal and API. Conductor's existing services are winding down in stages: new sign-ups halted immediately, Pro features were made free, Conductor Cloud goes read-only on November 13 and shuts down on November 20 (with workspace migration or data export options and subscriber refunds), and local Mac app copies will function until an unspecified new interface arrives in early 2027. Conductor stated it has never sold user data or trained models on user code and will delete stored workspace data after the shutdown dates.
takeaways: **Acquisition Details:** Meta acquired AI coding startup Conductor, whose desktop app runs multiple coding agents simultaneously in isolated codebase copies, with terms undisclosed.

**Supported Agents & Architecture:** The software integrates external agents including Anthropic Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Cursor, while Conductor Cloud utilizes sandboxed virtual machines for multi-hour tasks accessible via an iPhone app.

**Traction & Funding:** Founded as Melty Inc. in 2024 by Charlie Holtz and Jackson de Campos, Conductor raised a $22 million Series A in March from Spark Capital and Matrix and surpassed 100,000 users, including engineering teams at Meta, Google, and Spotify.

**Wind-Down Timeline:** Conductor stopped new sign-ups immediately, will transition its cloud service to read-only on November 13 before shutting down entirely on November 20, and plans to retire current local Mac apps in early 2027.

title: Nothing CEO says company’s mysterious AI-first device is dropping next month
author: Lucas Ropek
contentSnippet: Nothing, the smartphone startup behind the distinctive Nothing Phone , is working on an AI product, but what it is remains unclear. On Wednesday, CEO Carl Pei posted on X that the company’s first “AI-native product” ships in December. “It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product. It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app,” Pei wrote. Pei has teased an AI-first device for some time and the company has also said that it plans to release a pair of AI-linked smart glasses, as well as earbuds with AI integrations. Pei’s description adds up to a screenless non-app that uses AI? He also calls it a “productivity tool.” Adding further mystique to the announcement, Pei seems to downplay any link to AI wearables. “The whole industry is hunting for its iPhone moment: the pendant, the pin, the glasses, the companion, some magical consumer device that makes AI part of everyone’s life,” Pei wrote. “I admire the boldness, but I read this moment differently.” No firm release date has been announced, but Nothing fans should know soon enough what the company has in store for them. title: Almost no one uses AI agents to book their Uber, company says
author: Sarah Perez
contentSnippet:
Very few people are using personal AI agents to order Ubers, apparently. On the transportation giant’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, the company said that only four rides were ordered through an AI agent during its busiest week in October: the week of Halloween.

While more people used an AI agent to order food through its delivery service, Uber Eats, the volume was still fairly small compared to the overall number of trips.

Uber’s chief financial officer, Balaji Krishnamurthy, told Wall Street analysts on the call that the company handled around 320 million trips and orders across Uber and Uber Eats during the week of Halloween, but only 500 Uber Eats orders were placed by an AI agent.

“It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” said CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, referring to the low number of orders placed by AI agents. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.”

The surprisingly low numbers of AI-initiated transactions come amid growing hype for a new wave of AI agents that don’t just answer questions but also handle tasks on users’ behalf. There’s been an explosion of personal AI startups, including one of the buzziest, Instinct, which was founded last year and raised its most recent round of funding at a $10 billion valuation. Meta’s Muse also became the No. 1 app in Apple’s U.S. App Store last month, topping 10 million users, per Meta’s own reporting . The company said many were using it to shop and transact with businesses.

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and SpaceXAI (Grok) are also now offering their own AI agents, as are numerous smaller startups.

Still, early numbers from public companies indicate the agentic web still has a long way to go. DoorDash, for instance, said last week on its earnings call that it has only received a few hundred orders from AI agents so far, as most customers are still placing orders through the DoorDash app.

Uber is seeing the same behavior, it seems. Khosrowshahi pointed out that the average time to book a ride is only 50 seconds in the company’s app, and re-ordering a favorite food only takes 90 seconds. That suggests an AI agent isn’t necessarily saving anyone time.

Despite the low number of AI-driven transactions, Khosrowshahi seemed bullish on the idea of agents in general. “We think that is another opportunity to reach our platform. We think it will be a net positiv

summary.tldr:
Uber reported minimal consumer adoption of AI agents for ride-hailing and food delivery during its Q3 earnings call. During the week of Halloween, which saw a total of 320 million trips and orders across the Uber platform, only four rides were booked via AI agents. Uber Eats saw slightly higher, yet still negligible, volume with 500 orders placed by AI agents during the same period.

CEO Dara Khosrowshahi attributed the low adoption to the high efficiency of the existing Uber app, noting that booking a ride takes an average of 50 seconds, while re-ordering food takes 90 seconds, leaving little room for AI agents to provide significant time savings. Despite these figures, Uber remains engaged with approximately eight major AI assistant providers and expects that number to exceed 10, viewing the technology as a potential long-term demand driver for the platform.
takeaways: **Q3 Performance Metrics:** Uber processed 320 million total trips and orders during the week of Halloween, with only 4 rides and 500 Uber Eats orders initiated by AI agents.
**Competitive Context:** DoorDash reported similar trends, noting only a few hundred orders placed via AI agents to date.
**User Friction Analysis:** Uber leadership argues that current app workflows are already highly optimized, with ride booking averaging 50 seconds and food re-ordering averaging 90 seconds.
**Market Outlook:** Uber is currently in discussions with roughly eight major AI assistant companies and anticipates the number of available agents to grow beyond 10.

title: AI agents meet billable hours as Certinia rethinks services delivery
author: Mark Albertson
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 16:55 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026

AI agents meet billable hours as Certinia rethinks services delivery

Certinia Inc. is bringing AI into the software firms use to sell projects, assign staff, deliver work and bill clients.

AI’s ability to instantaneously draw from a deep well of information and provide guidance in practically any field of expertise has changed the paradigm for professional services. For Certinia Inc., whose business facilitates 7.1 billion professional services operations per month, AI represents a significant opportunity for its clients.

“I think the only industry that’s probably been more disrupted by AI than the technology industry has probably been the services industry,” Robert Cesafsky , chief operating officer of Certinia, told theCUBE . “Whether you are a software company, a hardware company, a tax and accounting firm [or] management consulting … all of these industries are being directly targeted or impacted by AI. Platform for professional services

Certinia’s Salesforce-native platform connects a wide range of processes spanning sales, project delivery, financial management and customer success. The company’s approach helps clients transform cost centers into profit centers by improving visibility into customer activities, optimizing resource deployment and maintaining connectivity throughout the customer lifecycle.

“We can take away all the administrative tasks and outsource that to AI in order to help them deliver faster time outcomes, but it also helps them deliver a lower cost to serve that project,” said Mimi Spier , chief marketing officer of Certinia, in an interview with theCUBE. “We can identify expansion opportunities, [and] at-risk customers where we need to opt

summary.tldr: Certinia Inc., formerly known as FinancialForce.com, is integrating AI-driven automation into its professional services platform to manage project delivery, staffing, and billing. The company, which facilitates 7.1 billion professional services operations monthly, has launched 'Veda,' an enterprise-grade intelligent operations engine. Veda is designed to automate administrative tasks, identify expansion opportunities, and manage at-risk customer renewals, aiming to transform services from cost centers into profit centers by lowering the cost-to-serve and accelerating project outcomes.
takeaways: **Veda Agent Expansion:** Certinia launched Veda in April with 10 package agents, grew to 24 by late 2026, and plans to exceed 40 by the end of the year.
**System of Action Scaling:** In September 2026, Certinia expanded its 'System of Action' for services, increasing its library of Veda Intelligent Actions from 64 to 135.

**Moonnox Acquisition:** The July 2026 acquisition of Moonnox added knowledge graphs and persistent project memory to Veda, allowing the platform to synthesize unstructured data (emails, chats, calls) with structured records like timecards.

**Architectural Framework:** The System of Action utilizes a three-tier architecture: data aggregation (structured/unstructured), institutional knowledge application (17+ years of data), and autonomous agent execution within existing workflows.
**Salesforce Integration:** Certinia remains a Salesforce-native platform and is listed under the AI agents and tools category for Salesforce’s AgentExchange.

title: 17 better ways Elon Musk could have wasted $446 million
author: Elizabeth Lopatto
contentSnippet: One of the basic problems of spending too much time on social media is that you are cooking your brain by reading posts from a pack of attention-seeking lunatics. If your social media of choice is the site formerly known as Twitter, and it is your main source of contact with the outside world, you may delusionally throw away nearly $500 million dollars on midterm elections, just like Elon Musk. In particular, $47 million of that money from Musk’s America PAC was aimed at defeating Texas Democrat James Talarico, who trounced Musk’s preferred Senate candidate, Ken Paxton, with 55 percent of the vote. Talarico even made Musk’s influence a central part of his campaign ads, with the slogan “Texas is not for sale.” How did Musk get this so wrong? I blame the bubble of X. My former colleague Casey Newton, who has (with some well-earned shame) slunk back to X, explained that he did so because it was the site that was most influential with the AI crowd. In some sense, this is exactly the problem. The agentmaxxing loons of AI influencing are wildly out of touch with normal people. There is, right now, one very important bipartisan position in the United States, and it is: Fuck a data center. It’s pretty obvious that the opposition to data centers is a way of making concrete how pissed off most people are with the tech industry, particularly with the gangster tech regulation of late and the constant stream of threats coming from AI companies. These guys have really tied themselves and their AI aspirations to Donald Trump’s sinking ship, and if you’re hanging out on X all the time, that’s impossible to see, not least because the site’s owner, Musk, is shaping the algorithm in ways that make him feel good. title: OpenAI to acquire developer tooling startup Pierre Computer
author: Maria Deutscher
contentSnippet: OpenAI Group PBC today announced plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company Inc., a low-profile developer tooling startup. The terms of the deal were not disclosed. Observers pegged it as a shot at Microsoft Corp.’s open-source software repository GitHub for the age of artificial intelligence agents. Pierre operates a cloud service that AI agents can use […] The post OpenAI to acquire developer tooling startup Pierre Computer appeared first on SiliconANGLE .

summary.tldr:
OpenAI Group PBC has announced plans to acquire developer tooling startup Pierre Computer Company Inc. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed by the companies. Pierre operates a cloud service designed for AI agents to store generated code, licenses, and interface design elements, which reportedly helped customer Lovable Inc. cut code retrieval latency by approximately 70%. Observers have framed the move as a competitive step against Microsoft Corp.'s GitHub.

As part of the transaction, OpenAI will absorb Pierre's team to help ship new products and platforms focused on optimizing coding agents, specifically streamlining Git workflows. Pierre already develops open-source libraries named Trees and Diffs, which currently underpin the interface of OpenAI's Codex programming tool. Trees facilitates folder navigation sidebars with search, drag-and-drop controls, and flags for recently added or updated files, while Diffs highlights specific changed lines of code either in-line or in a separate interface section. OpenAI confirmed it will continue offering Trees and Diffs under open-source licenses post-acquisition, while integrating Pierre's paid code hosting service into Codex.

In parallel with the acquisition announcement, OpenAI disclosed details regarding an internal software engine called Pando, built to optimize its internal Git environment and reduce the time required for coding agents to create and read code files.
takeaways: **Acquisition Target:** OpenAI Group PBC announced plans to acquire developer tooling startup Pierre Computer Company Inc. for an undisclosed sum.
**Performance Metric:** Pierre's cloud storage service for AI-generated code helped customer Lovable Inc. reduce code retrieval latency by roughly 70%.

**Open-Source Integration:** Pierre-developed libraries Trees and Diffs currently power the folder navigation and file-diffing interfaces of OpenAI's Codex programming tool and will remain open-source.
**Internal Infrastructure:** OpenAI uses an internal software engine named Pando to enhance the performance of its Git environment for coding agents.

title: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor
author: Lucas Ropek
contentSnippet:
Meta has acquired Conductor , an AI coding startup that allows users to spin up software projects by deploying multiple agents into parallel workspaces.

The news was originally reported by Axios, and Conductor shared news of its acquisition on its blog.

“I have big news: Conductor is joining Meta,” wrote the startup’s founder and CEO, Charlie Holtz, on Wednesday. “We have some big, crazy plans for the next interface,” he added, teasing that the company would have “something new” for customers to use by “early next year.”

On X, Holtz also noted that he was looking forward to working with Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, and Nat Friedman, head of product at the company’s Superintelligence Labs. “They’ve been on an absolute tear, and I’m convinced MSL has the highest talent density of all the labs,” he added.

Meta confirmed the acquisition to TechCrunch but wouldn’t comment further or provide additional details about the deal.

Conductor, founded in 2024, only launched its core product just last summer. The company’s agentic teams, which can be deployed in the cloud, locally, or via a user’s phone, are designed to help software engineers work on separate, compartmentalized parts of a project in concert. The agents that the platform deploys aren’t developed in-house but come from major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI.

Holtz said that, until early next year, Conductor’s core features would continue to work as they previously have. The exception is Conductor’s cloud service, which will shut down on November 20, after which the company will begin deleting user cloud data.

Meta, which previously lagged behind in AI services, has spent the last several months trying to catch up. In August, the company launched Muse Code , its own coding agent. Meanwhile, the company’s recently launched Muse agents are seeing significant adoption, with the company recently reporting that the service had surpassed 10 million users. The company has also made a number of AI-related acquisitions over the past year, including Moltbook , the viral agent platform that made headlines.

title: Ricursive AI Releases Ripple-65B Preview: A 65B Dense Open-Weight Model Scoring 80.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1
author: Asif Razzaq
contentSnippet: Ricursive Intelligence just released Ripple-65B Preview . Ripple-65B Preview is a 65B dense open-weight model from Ricursive, pretrained from scratch for agentic coding. It is a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model behind Ricursive’s AI chip design platform. The main claim: 80.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 , the top self-reported score among US open-weight models. Every MoE rival it beats on that test carries 501B to 975B total parameters. TL;DR Size: 65B dense (65B active), pretrained on 12T tokens, up to 1M context. Runs on: BF16 on datacenter GPUs (250 tok/s on 2x B200). Experimental NVFP4 build targets NVIDIA DGX Spark. Performance: Frontier-level agentic coding for its size; trails larger MoE models on knowledge and science coding. Best: Terminal-Bench 2.1, 80.5 (self-reported). Worst: SciCode, 39.4, lowest of the 5 models in Ricursive’s own table. What is Ripple-65B Preview? The release includes 3 checkpoints : an instruction-tuned BF16 model, an NVFP4 version , and a BF16 base model . All ship under Apache 2.0. Pretraining used a text-only corpus, mostly English and code, at 8K sequence length. Ricursive team states that the full R&D cost was $32M . That figure covers ladder experiments, data mixing, evals, synthetic data and the final runs. Ricursive team estimates that it is one-tenth the cost of the prior open-weight agentic coding leader. How does the architecture work? Ricursive chose a dense Transformer over Mixture-of-Experts to reduce infrastructure complexity. Training held 40% MFU with simple sharding, no custom kernels and no quantization. The model is thin and deep: a d_model of 5120 across 80 layers. It moves from Olmo 3’s Llama-like layout to a Gemma 3N-like design for stability. Key choices: Overprovisioned attention heads for reasoning, offset by more sliding-window layers and smaller windows. Gated attention , global NoPE and value residuals . FFN activation clipping , a technique also used in gpt-oss . Ricursive team built the recipe through laddering experiments starting from Olmo 3’s ladder . It rejected changes that failed to hold at 4B scale, such as 2-stream mHC. The technical post reports a 16x code compute-efficiency gain at 4B scale. How was it post-trained? Post-training ran midtraining, long context, SFT, long-context SFT and mixed RL. Long-context stages trained at 2M sequence length. Ricursive bought no post-traini

title: Research prediction: Shift from digital banking to AI-driven finance will transform financial services in 2027
author: Mark Albertson
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 15:40 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026

Research prediction: Shift from digital banking to AI-driven finance will transform financial services in 2027

The coming year will signal an abrupt transition from digital banking to intelligent finance, as AI agents and operating models reshape the ways that financial firms acquire customers and provide advice.

This is the central thesis of a new Forrester Research report , “Predictions 2027: Banking and Investing.” The findings were summarized from data involving 915 respondents in the U.S., U.K., and Canada.

Forrester identified several key points of transition. These included fundamental changes through automation in financial discovery and guidance journeys, as well as a belief that although one-third of banks will announce an AI transformation program, only 5% will succeed.

“In 2027, financial services will enter a new phase in which intelligence becomes the primary source of value creation,” said Forrester researchers in the report. “AI assistants are reshaping how customers discover, evaluate and act on financial products; investment participation is expanding despite persistent economic anxiety; and banks are racing to determine whether AI will merely enhance existing operations or fundamentally transform them.”

Scaling AI for financial services

Forrester’s prediction of a 5% success rate is based on a belief that many banks will rebrand existing AI initiatives as AI-native without significant changes in operational infrastructure. Retention of legacy processes and operating models will prevent an ability to scale AI deployment, a fundamental requirement that AI technology providers such as Dell Technologies Inc. are emphasizing to their clients in the financial services world.

“Ultimately, I think we’ve enough proof points now that AI works and it works really well and it gives you speed and efficiency in your company,” according to David Kennedy , chief financial officer of Dell, during a recent interview with theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. “The question is, can you do that at scale?”

One way that financial institutions will pursue scale is through mergers and acquisitions. Forrester predicts that AI banking technology M&A will increase by 50% in 2027. Acquisition of proprietary data assets, governance capabilities, and AI-native orchestration will require an ability to navigate h

summary.tldr:
Forrester Research’s "Predictions 2027: Banking and Investing" report, based on data from 915 respondents across the U.S., U.K., and Canada, forecasts a transition from digital banking to AI-driven finance. The report predicts that while 33% of banks will announce AI transformation programs in 2027, only 5% are expected to succeed. This low success rate is attributed to the tendency of institutions to rebrand existing initiatives as "AI-native" without updating legacy infrastructure or operational models, which Forrester identifies as a critical barrier to scaling AI deployment.

To achieve scale, Forrester anticipates a 50% increase in AI banking technology mergers and acquisitions in 2027, driven by the need for proprietary data assets and AI-native orchestration. Concurrently, 40% of banks are expected to launch AI assistants next year. Industry leaders from Dell Technologies Inc. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. emphasize that competitive advantage will not stem from the models themselves, but from the integration of proprietary knowledge and the ability to host open-weight models in hybrid, on-premises environments to maintain data sovereignty.
takeaways: **Success Rate Forecast:** Only 5% of banks announcing AI transformation programs in 2027 are projected to succeed due to reliance on legacy processes.
**M&A Activity:** AI banking technology mergers and acquisitions are predicted to rise by 50% in 2027 as firms seek proprietary data and governance capabilities.
**AI Assistant Adoption:** 40% of banks are expected to launch AI assistants in 2027 to facilitate customer discovery and financial guidance.
**Strategic Moats:** Dell CTO John Roese identifies proprietary institutional knowledge, rather than specific models or tools, as the primary competitive moat for financial firms.
**Infrastructure Requirements:** AMD and Dell emphasize that scaling AI requires hybrid computing environments capable of hosting open-weight models on-premises.

title: Gemini for Home now plugs into AT&T’s smart security system
